notes: §1985:VI.6.24.3 SR1: "Literal-1 must not be a figurative constant that begins with the word ALL." ControlFlowBinder.BindStop calls ScreenStopLiteral, which runs where the STOP literal statement exists (Constructs.StopLiteralRemoved2002: 85 only) and reports COBOL6817 when the literal's figurativeConstant carries ALL; the witness is STOP ALL "A". Probes (work-rd-09/stop): b) refused COBOL6817: ALL "A", ALL 'XY', ALL ZERO, ALL SPACES, ALL QUOTES, ALL symbolic-character, 1.5, 1.0, .5, -1, +1; accepted and run: ZERO, SPACE, QUOTE, HIGH-VALUE, "HELLO", 0, the 18-digit 123456789012345678 (each printed, then 'AFTER'); c) X"41" is COBOL0900 at 85, and the whole STOP literal statement is COBOL0902 at --std 2002. Outside this rule (the general format with §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.3): STOP BEL, a symbolic-character without ALL, is refused as parse error COBOL5506 ('expected &') though DISPLAY BEL compiles; no kb/Work note found for it.

next.reason: 1985: "Literal-1 must not be a figurative constant that begins with the word ALL."; 2023: "STOP rules only say: "If literal-1 is numeric, it shall be an integer." and "Literal-1 shall not be a zero-length literal."". The 2023 STOP syntax rules still cover literal-1, but none of them bars a figurative constant that begins with ALL. The 1985 restriction is dropped.
